title: You Might Be a Micromanager If
author: Admired Leadership
summary: Modeled on comedian Jeff Foxworthy's "you might be a redneck" format, this article delivers a humorous but pointed list of ten "tells" that reveal micromanaging behavior. Beneath the jokes, it makes a serious point: micromanagers dictate nearly every move of the people they lead, robbing them of the independent action and risk-taking essential for development, and most micromanagers remain genuinely unaware of the pattern. The lighthearted format is used deliberately to make an uncomfortable form of self-recognition easier to absorb.
points: The article borrows Jeff Foxworthy's "you might be a redneck" format to deliver a humorous list of micromanagement tells.
Micromanagement is defined as dictating and controlling nearly every move of the people being led.
This controlling style robs team members of independent action and risk-taking necessary for growth.
Most micromanagers remain unaware they exhibit the pattern, much like the subjects of Foxworthy's original jokes.
The humorous format is a deliberate device for making self-recognition of an uncomfortable trait easier to accept.
quotes: The comedian Jeff Foxworthy delighted his fans in the 1990s with a never-ending string of one-liners about how to tell if they might be a redneck.
Micromanagers dictate and control nearly every move of those they lead and manage.
Their controlling nature robs team members of the independent action, risk-taking, and creative problem-solving essential for personal development.
You might be a micromanager if the frequency with which you check on the progress of an assignment is best measured in seconds and minutes.
You might be a micromanager if the team has created a special therapy group to work through their issues with your leadership style.
